sources.entry: MKVPriority - Selects preferred audio and subtitle tracks using configurable priority scores and sets the appropriate default and forced flags. MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: MKVPriority is a Python/Docker tool that scores audio and subtitle tracks in MKV files and sets default and forced flags in place using mkvpropedit, without remuxing.
summary.what_it_does: MKVPriority assigns configurable priority scores to audio and subtitle tracks based on properties such as language, codec, and track name filters. It then sets the default and forced flags on the highest-scoring tracks and clears them on lower-priority ones, editing the MKV headers in place with mkvpropedit rather than remuxing. It estimates forced subtitles using dialogue-density heuristics and can suppress default subtitle flags when the native audio is playing. External sidecar subtitles are scored alongside embedded tracks, and their filenames can be updated to match. The tool runs as a CLI, as a Docker image, or as a cron-scheduled job with an archive database to skip already-processed files. Radarr and Sonarr can call it through a custom script on import or upgrade. Optional extension modules add post-processing such as subtitle extraction, conversion, restyling, renaming, and multiplexing.
use_cases: set Japanese audio and ASS subtitles as default in anime libraries
automatically pick the right audio and subtitle track in MKV movies
process new files as Radarr or Sonarr imports them
batch-update flags across an existing media library on a cron schedule
extract default or forced subtitles to external files for players with limited support
deprioritize commentary or dub tracks in MKV files
notable: Edits MKV track flags in place with mkvpropedit, so no remuxing is needed
Scores tracks like Radarr/Sonarr custom formats, configured via TOML files
Heuristic forced-subtitle detection that does not rely only on track names
Extension module system with example subtitle extractor, converter, restyler, renamer, and multiplexer
Tag-based multiple configs that map to Radarr/Sonarr tags
caveats: Requires MKVToolNix installed for the CLI; Docker image avoids this
Changing file metadata can break hardlinks
Multiplexer and subtitle extraction features are optional extension modules that must be enabled
Radarr/Sonarr integration requires the script to be visible inside the container and mount paths to match
